entities.name: the 汴河 at the grain wharf (汴水悍激)
entities.what: The 汴河 along the east wharves: open water left as plain silk and drawn all over with long, flowing, roughly horizontal current lines, curling crests and eddy spirals (汴水悍激, "the Bian's fierce current"); boats moored along its north bank: the mat-cabin boat west of the great willow, the two grain boats (万石船) and a smaller boat south of the second one. No south bank is painted: the silk's bottom edge cuts the water. At the east end the water runs out under the massive willow at the bottom right.
entities.vis: part: the moored boats hide the north shore from u 26000 to 26790 and from 27245 to 28720; willow whips and the massive willow's head hide it east of 28400
entities.note: No shore is inked. shore_n is read where the bank's ink-wash smudges end and the thin wavy current lines begin. West of the great willow it is hidden behind the mat-cabin boat (the bank in front of the warehouse shows only to v 640-650, where the boat's roof begins; est v 655-680; the true line could lie anywhere down to about v 850 behind the hull). East of the boat's stern the first current lines show at (26815, 890); the shore then runs down the wash-drawn bank below the willow and the jetty to v 1040-1110 (u 26960-27150; a dark wash tongue reaches v ~1150 at u 27100-27225). OTHER READING at the willow: t8/t9 put the willow's roots (27068, 905) at the water's edge, which would lift the shore there by about 150 px; I read the smudges at v 930-1100 below the roots as bank wash, not water (conf low). Behind the grain boats it is est at the boats' north gunwales (v 1110-1160); at u 28297-28357 it is t11's edge line under the bank porter (v 1203-1234); east of 28400 under willow whips and the massive willow's knobbed head (est). EAST END: the line turns south along the massive willow's west foot and meets the silk's bottom edge at about (28968, 1780, est), just east of the bottom boat's rudder tip (28955, 1768) and west of the willow's roots (u 28942-29255, v 1725-1787): no water is painted east of the willow (bare silk with bank wash at u 29150-29400, v 1450-1780), so the water does not reach the S1 seam at 29050. WEST END: (26000, 665, est), hidden behind the mat-cabin boat; river_m's line continues west. No shore_s: the silk's bottom edge (v ~1780 at u 26200-28700, measured) cuts the water all along the reach. 汴水悍激 (pin 7, u 26670): the current lines fill u 26000-27270 from v ~1000 (below the mat-cabin boat; from v ~890 east of its stern) to the silk's edge, densest and longest at v 1050-1500; eddy spirals at (26300, 1185) (a large one, rings over u 26120-26415, v 1155-1210), (26680, 1222), (27022, 1223) and (26908, 1495); thinner lines continue under and between the grain boats (u 27270-28100, v 1500-1780). The restyle's east half paints u 25500-26400 v 1000-1790 as dry grassy ground (its first draw, kept): it is water on the scan.

entities.name: north bank of the 汴河 at the east wharves
entities.what: The river's north bank from the warehouse to the massive willow: a narrow strip in front of the warehouse and its plain wall where the mat-cabin boat lies close in, then a broad wash-drawn slope under the great willow, the jetty and the eating sheds, down to the grain boats, with the porters' mooring stakes on its top and the bank porter climbing it from the second grain boat; no revetment, stair or vertical face.
entities.vis: part: the boats, the jetty, the great willow's trunk and the willow whips cover much of it
entities.note: bank_top is where the level ground ends: the warehouse plinth's foot (v 628-632 at u 26000-26230; t7 reads the bank strip at v 555-640) and the plain wall's front (v ~640 at 26450); under the great willow's knob head (est, its lower edge at (26890, 676)); from u 27100 to 27400 the jetty's deck edge (the jetty stands at the top of the slope, its posts' feet on the slope); the lower shed's front and t10's mooring stake on the bank top (27902, 985); t11 reads the top at v 970-985 over u 28100-28400; est under the willows further east. The slope between bank_top and shore is narrow in the west (hidden behind the boat) and 250-300 px of v deep at u 26900-28400 (a long gentle slope, not a face). Bank top taken at street level (H 0). Things on the bank are the tiles' (t8-t12) and structures_e's; the wattle fence under the knob head (26850-26970, v 625-662) is left to structures_e. FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like the river's shores; its bank_top on the ground.

entities.name: raised plank walkway (jetty) in front of the lower shed
entities.what: A raised plank deck on posts running along the top of the bank in front of the lower eating shed, from behind the great willow's trunk (u ~27080) east to u ~27420: its river-facing front edge has a lattice railing or fascia of short vertical slats, and four posts stand on the bank slope below it; the shed's tables stand on or just behind it. Nobody is on it (t9). It does not reach the water: the wash-drawn bank continues 50-200 px below its posts' feet.
entities.vis: part: the great willow's trunk hides its west end; the shed's posts and tables stand behind it
entities.note: ON LAND, NOT OVER WATER: the posts' feet are on the bank slope (v 842-947) and the water's edge is lower, at v ~1070-1135 (u 27050-27250). The brief leaves a wholly-on-land jetty to structures_e, but structures_e's brief gives the jetty to river_e and t9 lists it as river_e's, so I record it so it is not missed; if structures_e records it (or reads it as the lower shed's raised floor), the merge keeps one. Strokes: front top edge (27135, 765) -> (27380, 850), slope +0.35; a lower rail about 40 px below it with short vertical slats between (a railing or the deck's fascia); posts (bays) at u 27135, 27225, 27316 and 27385, feet at v 842, 895, 926 and 947 (+-10 px); the east end at about u 27400-27420, the west end behind the willow trunk at about u 27080-27100 (est). The north corners are placeholders (the deck's back edge is under the shed's tables). SCALE CUE: front edge 77-97 px above the posts' feet (765 -> 842 at u 27135; 850 -> 947 at u 27380). Reading of the top line as the deck edge (with the restyle, which draws a plank floor there with tables on it): conf med; the other reading is that the top line is a railing's top rail and the deck lies about 40 px lower. The restyle paves the bank below it with flagstones: not painted. For the tiles' support `jetty deck: S2.str.jetty`, read this ID.

entities.name: big cabin boat with mat roofs moored by the warehouse
entities.what: A big timber boat moored along the north bank west of the great willow, bow west: a deep planked hull with nail rows; a gable-roofed fore cabin (u 26040-26150) and a long flat-roofed cabin with plank walls and doors behind it to u ~26530, a ladder leaning against the cabin side from the deck to the roof (26255, 840)-(26200, 720), a row of round coiled bundles (rolled mats or rope coils; the restyle draws tied netted baskets) along a woven-mat cover behind the roof (v 650-700), and a long pole lying along the roof (u 26330-26565, v ~645: a spare spar or punting pole); aft, a barrel-vaulted woven-mat hood (u 26490-26700, v 610-720) with three big round bundles, an open arched mat hood over the after deck (u 26700-26800) with a man in its mouth, a raised stern gallery with a lattice rail and an overhanging stern (tip (26845, 707)); under the stern a big rudder on a stock with a drum-shaped head, its lattice blade reaching down and aft into the water. A post with a round head stands on deck at (26365, 725). No mooring line or sweep is drawn. Its bow is hidden behind the stern and rudder of river_m's boat moored just west of it (u 25150-26050).
entities.vis: part: the bow is hidden behind river_m's boat's stern and rudder (u 25850-26100); the great willow's whips cross the stern hood
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder hangs under the east end (stock at u 26616, head (26600-26645, 870-892), blade u 26600-26790, v 920-1048), and the east end carries the raised stern gallery: stern east, bow west, facing 175 (the hull rises slightly toward the bow). t9 calls the east end the "bow": it is the stern. FRONT is est: the hull's strakes run west behind river_m's boat's rudder (u 25990-26100) with no sign of a stem east of u 26060; a foredeck ahead of the fore cabin (front u 26040) puts the stem at about u 25930-26030. REAR = the waterline under the sternpost where the rudder hangs (the hull's bottom line runs (26075, 970), (26262, 989), (26450, 995), (26606, 1001)); the stern overhangs it by 245 px at deck level. SCALE CUE: hull 25980 (est) to 26845 (overhang) = about 865 px; waterline length front-rear 620 px; freeboard at u 26300: deck edge v 835 (below the cabin walls' foot at 822-831) -> waterline v 990 = 155 px; cabin walls about 95 px (735 -> 830); fore cabin door about 70 px; rudder blade about 190 px long. The hull is drawn deep: this boat rides high (no cargo in the hull). Waterline evidence: the dark bottom strake with current lines below it from v ~1000 and the rudder blade entering the water. Possible mooring: the capped posts t7 reads at u 26018 and 26128 (v 565-630) stand at the warehouse plinth's foot; no rope from this boat reaches them (zoom 3), so they look like the plinth's pillar feet.

entities.name: boatman crouching on the cabin roof
entities.what: A boatman in a dark cap crouching or squatting on the front edge of the long cabin's roof, bent forward among the coiled bundles, a hatched (straw or padded) garment over his lower body; boat crew, working at the bundles.
entities.note: Strokes: figure u 26265-26317, v 672-714 (dark head and back, hatched lower part); the cabin roof's front edge at v ~716-720 under him; the boat's deck edge v 835 and the waterline v 990 straight below. Painted about 42 px crouched. Facing is not readable (back or side view): 180 taken from the hat at his west end. The restyle paints a seated man in blue with a white headcloth here. The tall light shape at (26337-26350, 733-838) beside the cabin door is a door leaf or a board standing on end, not a figure.

entities.name: man in the mouth of the stern hood
entities.what: A man (head and one arm) looking out of the open arched mat hood over the after deck, seated or leaning on the hood's floor; boat crew or the steersman resting.
entities.vis: part: only the head and an arm show inside the hood
entities.note: Strokes: a head with a face at (26753-26770, 627-647) and a hand or arm at (26720-26757, 650-677) inside the hood u 26715-26795, v 625-700; the hood's floor (the raised after deck) at v ~700-705. t8 reads the same figure (26722-26755, v 640-678) and the restyle paints a face there. OTHER READING: coiled rope or bundled gear inside the hood (the strokes are faint); kept because two readings and the restyle agree. Waterline straight below at about v 1000 (est; the stern overhangs the water), so this after deck stands about 300 px above the water: a high poop. Painted about 74 px from the head to the hood floor. FRAME: support -> `boat stern deck: S2.veh.boat_mat_cabin_25980`: he sits on the high after deck under the stern hood (river_e: (26750, ~702) over the waterline ~1000 est, 298 px), not on the main deck (155 px).

entities.name: the mat-cabin boat and its crew
entities.what: The big mat-roofed cabin boat moored by the warehouse, with a boatman crouching on its cabin roof and a man in its stern hood.

entities.name: grain boat (万石船) with the gangplank
entities.what: A big, broad, deep-laden grain boat moored with its rounded bow to the north-west against the bank and its stern toward the viewer: at the bow two overlapping woven-mat roofs (u 27280-27750, v 1000-1110) over a small deckhouse with windows and posts (u 27560-27750); a long spar lying fore-and-aft along the deck (u 27490-27810, v 1128-1147: the lowered mast or a windlass beam); planked hatch covers (u 27305-27500, v 1195-1295) and the cargo under nets of crossing ropes amidships; a high transom stern with an arched gallery roof (u 27760-28010, v 1155-1220), a tiller bar (v 1265-1280) and a big rudder hanging from its centre, the blade reaching (28086, 1593). A cleated gangplank runs from its north gunwale near the stern (27795, 1145) up the bank to (28023, 1050) (nobody on it), and two mooring lines run from the gunwale beside it up to t10's rope coil and stake on the bank top (S2.prop.coiled_rope_27873, S2.prop.mooring_stake_27902). Moored stern to bow with the second grain boat (S2.veh.boat_grain_28095).
entities.vis: part: its north side lies against the bank; the stern's lower part is hidden by the rudder
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder hangs from the east end's transom (stock u 27880-27900 from v 1217 down to the water at ~1500; blade to (28086, 1593)): stern east, toward the viewer; the rounded west end with the mat roofs is the bow. Facing 160: from rear (27882, 1505) to front (27285, 1330) the axis climbs 175 px of v, so the bow points west-north-west into the bank. FRONT est: the bow is round; the outer hull line runs (27268, 1230) -> (27293, 1330) -> (27357, 1400) -> (27464, 1464) -> (27571, 1493) -> (27793, 1514), and the waterline under the stem is taken at (27285, 1330). SCALE CUE: hull 27267-28010 (743 px over all, front-rear 600 px along u); beam seen at the bow from the north gunwale (v ~1120) to the south waterline (v ~1450) at u 27400; freeboard amidships low (deep-laden): south gunwale v ~1440 -> waterline 1493 at u 27570 = 53 px; transom about 250 px wide (u 27760-28010). Gangplank: two rails about 15 px apart with 7-8 cleats, 245 px long. Ropes: two parallel lines from the coil (27885, 982) down the bank to (27865, 1123) and to the gunwale at about (27845, 1150); a frayed end trails east from the coil to (27940, 1003) (t10's). The restyle draws the same boat (blue mats, a windlass) and no crowd on deck.

entities.name: steersman (?) at the grain boat's rudder head
entities.what: A dark round head with a cap showing above the tiller bar under the stern gallery's arch, as of a man standing at the rudder head; boatman or steersman. Possibly only the rudder stock's rounded head.
entities.vis: part: only the head shows, behind the tiller bar
entities.note: Strokes: a dark rounded blob (27877-27903, v 1222-1245) on the centreline of the transom, on top of the rudder stock and above the tiller bar (v 1265-1280). The restyle paints a man in a blue cap here and a second, white-robed figure at (27813-27857, 1247-1273), where the scan has only curved rope or rail lines (not recorded). OTHER READING: the rudder stock's rounded head (the bottom boat's and the mat-cabin boat's rudder heads look much the same, and t12 reads the bottom boat's as a mechanism). Stern deck est v 1300 under him; the waterline straight below at v ~1505. Second pass: still open (conf low kept). On a gridless zoom-2.5 crop the blob (u 27877-27907, v 1222-1246) is dome-topped with a flat brim, over a lighter patch at v 1246-1266 just above the tiller bar (v 1266-1278): it reads like a capped head over a face. The bottom boat's rudder head, where no man stands, is drawn differently: a squarish block with a hole, a windlass and ropes (n_bbrudder.jpg). The restyle's second, white-robed figure at (27813-27857, 1247-1273) is only the gallery's curved rails on the scan. FRAME: support -> `boat stern deck: S2.veh.boat_grain_27285`: the steersman reading stands on the stern deck by the tiller (river_e: ~v 1300 est over the waterline at rear (27882, 1505), 205 px), far above the deep-laden boat's gunwale amidships (53 px).

entities.name: the west grain boat and its crew
entities.what: The west grain boat (万石船) moored at the bank with its gangplank down to the shore, a man (?) at its rudder head; its grain is what the porters (t10's and t11's groups) carry ashore to the sack piles.
entities.note: The porters and the owner on the sacks are t10's group; t11's bank porter climbs from the second grain boat.

entities.name: second grain boat (万石船) under the willows
entities.what: A second laden grain boat moored east of the first, bow to bow-stern with it, bow west: a woven-mat hood with a coiled mat on its top over the bow (u 28015-28290, v 1160-1240), a cross beam and posts below it, the dark raked stem descending to the water; the hull and its mat-covered cargo run east under the willow whips; on the after deck (u 28480-28700, v 1280-1430) a pile of heavy coiled cables and a long bundle with two short dark uprights (bitts, or one man and his raised arm: see the low-confidence figure S2.fig.boatman_coils_28543) and a small windlass frame; the stern is hidden behind the massive willow's knobbed head. A ladder runs from its after deck down to the bottom boat (S2.veh.boat_bottom_28395); its mooring line goes to t11's post with a coiled rope at the bank's foot (S2.prop.mooring_post_rope_28272).
entities.vis: part: willow whips cover the hull from u 28150 east; the massive willow's head hides the stern; the bottom boat hides the south waterline
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder is not visible. The dark blade at the west end (28030, 1290) -> (28100, 1470) slopes DOWN and EAST (under the hull), as a raked stem does; a rudder hanging from a west stern would slope down and WEST (aft), as the three visible rudders here slope aft. So bow west (conf med; the restyle also paints a stem there). OTHER READING: the dark blade is a rudder and the west end the stern (t12 reads the east end's coils and windlass as the stern, which agrees with mine): then swap front/rear and facing 10. FRONT = the stem's foot at the water (28095, 1468); the stem head (28030, 1245) overhangs it 70 px west. REAR est at the massive willow's head (the after-deck gear ends about u 28680-28714). Facing 190: we see the bow hood's front face, so the bow turns a little toward the viewer. SCALE CUE: about 600 px front-rear along u (the first grain boat: 600); bow hood 275 px wide; freeboard aft about 50 px (after deck v ~1420 -> water est 1470). The bank porter of t11 (S2.fig.bank_porter_28355) climbs the bank above its mat roof (feet est (28355, 1226) on the bank, not on a plank). The ladder t11 records on the bank slope (S2.prop.ladder_28538, (28492, 1155) -> (28585, 1102)) does not reach this boat on the scan; it is t11's.

entities.name: boatman (?) among the coiled cables
entities.what: A tall dark upright with a flat top among the coiled cables on the second grain boat's after deck, read as a man in a dark cap (幞头) standing behind the coils; boat crew. Possibly a bitt (mooring post).
entities.vis: part: behind the coils and willow whips; only the head and cap read
entities.note: Strokes: a dark upright 11 px wide (28537-28549, v 1281-1316) with a flat cap-like top; coils below it at u 28500-28600, v 1290-1400. The setup agent counts one or two people here on the scan and the restyle paints a standing man in blue with a black cap on this spot (plus about seven invented others). OTHER READING: one of a pair of bitts at the stern with cables wound round them. Deck est v ~1405-1420 (the ladder's top at (28500, 1420)); waterline straight below est v 1470. Second pass: still one man or a bitt (conf low kept). The dark upright is 11-13 px wide (u 28537-28550) with a flat, two-lobed top at v 1280-1290 and a narrower dark stem down to v 1316, dark all the way, with no lighter face below the 'cap'. The heads of the figures painted at this size nearby are 17-33 px wide (the bank porter 25 px, the shed keeper 26 px), which favours a bitt; the restyle paints one man in a black cap with his hand raised to his face exactly here, which favours a man. See the retirement of boatman_coils_28562 (retired at the second pass).

entities.name: the second grain boat and its crew
entities.what: The second grain boat under the willows with one man (low confidence; or a bitt) among the coiled cables on its after deck.

entities.name: smaller boat at the bottom edge, rafted to the second grain boat
entities.what: A smaller planked boat lying south of the second grain boat at the silk's bottom edge, bow west under the willow whips: a plain hull with strakes and round bitts or cleats along the gunwale (u 28450-28600), a small upright structure on deck at u 28637-28668, an upswept stern (28738, 1578) over a planked transom gallery (u 28680-28812, v 1656-1725), and a big rudder: a stock with a drum-shaped head and ropes (u 28792-28853, v 1576-1676) and a battened blade reaching down and aft to (28955, 1768). A ladder leans from its deck (28575, 1545) up to the second grain boat's after deck (28500, 1420). No cargo or crew read.
entities.vis: part: willow whips cover the bow and most of the deck; the massive willow's head hangs over the stern
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder at the east end (stock u 28815, blade to (28955, 1768)) makes the east end the stern. The setup brief's "man at its east end (28790, v 1590-1680)" is the rudder head and stock with its ropes (t12 agrees; the restyle draws the same mechanism): no figure. The restyle crowds about eight people on and around this boat (u 28450-28870, v 1270-1630): invented. FRONT est: the hull's strakes and its dark lower edge show from u ~28400 east ((28400, 1699) -> (28675, 1724)); west of 28400 only willow whips are drawn, so the bow is at about 28390-28400, hidden. SCALE CUE: front-rear about 415 px; freeboard at u 28575: gunwale v ~1590 -> waterline v ~1715 = 125 px; rudder blade about 160 px long. The ladder (two rails with rungs, about 145 px long) is part of this boat (it may belong to the grain boat: either way river_e's). The rudder blade's tip at u 28955 is 95 px west of the S1 seam.

entities.name: light ribbed object under the willow limb
entities.what: A small, light, elongated object with cross ribs lying under the massive willow's lowest limb at the water's edge: a rolled mat or basket on the bank, or the end of a small boat.
entities.vis: part: willow whips and the knobbed head around it
entities.note: Strokes: u 28843-28913, v 1443-1473, ribbed like a mat or a small hull's frames. t12 left it to river_e. OTHER READING: the end of a small boat tucked in behind the bottom boat's stern (the restyle paints a small prow with a cabin here); if a second pass reads a hull, it becomes a vehicle on the water. The shore here is est (under the willow), so whether it lies on the bank or on the water is unsure.
